# Exit Options Review

⚠️ **Finance warning / Avertissement finance** : informational only, not investment advice. Comparing exit routes clarifies a decision, it does not guarantee proceeds: markets close, buyers walk, there is a real risk of loss and of a lower realisation than any route indicates, and no comparison here is a promise of return. Curated by Skill Harbor: the exit options review skill of the private equity pack in andreworia/claude-finance-skills. Use it when the fund is deciding how to exit, not whether, usually twelve to twenty-four months before the intended realisation, and again whenever something moves the decision (a debt market reopening or shutting, an unsolicited approach, a fund life running down, LPs pressing for DPI); run it before a bank is mandated, because once an advisor is appointed the process design is largely fixed. The method fixes the hold case first as the reference case, not a residual: two more years of ownership on the current trajectory, debt paid down, the exit multiple then assumed, and the resulting equity value discounted back at the fund cost of equity, because without that number no route can be judged against doing nothing. Every route (trade sale, sponsor-to-sponsor, IPO, continuation vehicle, continued hold) is then scored on the same four axes even where one looks obviously wrong: value as proceeds net to the fund at its ownership percentage after debt and transaction costs, never headline EV, certainty of completion at the indicated price...
